newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NSW COURT REFUSES EXTENDION FOR MOTHER
The New South Wales Supreme Court has refused to allow a Sydney woman an extension of time to sue the state over claims she was forced to give up her baby for adoption.
The 44-year-old woman, who gave birth to a son at 16, says her memories of the event did not re-surface until four years ago.
During the hearing, she claimed she was never allowed to see her newborn and was coerced into signing an adoption consent form while under sedation.
However, the court found found that because of the length of time since the birth, the state would not be able to properly defend her claim for damages and refused the application.
NATIONAL APPROACH TO SEX OFFENCES: PAPER
A discussion paper commissioned by federal and state Attorneys General has recommended paedophiles could be jailed for up to 25 years for sexual offences.
The paper canvasses options for a national approach to sex offences on key issues such as paedophilia, consent and making court processes less harrowing for victims of sexual abuse.
Attorney-General Daryl Williams says its release coincides with the release of an official survey suggesting up to 130-thousand women experienced sexual violence by men in the past year.
Mr Williams says the legislation would cover sexual assault on women and threats of sexual violence.
He says the aim is to develop a uniform approach to criminal law so all Australians have similar protection.
HANSON TREADS A SOFTER LINE
Federal independent M-P Pauline Hanson has told a rally of reitrees that she deplores racism and hatred.
Speaking on the Gold Coast, the controversial member for Oxley says Australians shouldn't encourage racial vilification, but should be able to voice an opinion in a civil manner.
Ms Hanson, acknowledged the importance of aboriginal culture to the national character of Australia.
She also said that she felt for Asians in the community who may be being suffering from racist treatment.
After the rally, Mrs Hanson said she would consider forming a new politicial party, but ruled out any association with expelled Western Australian liberal, Noel Crichton Browne.
NO QUIET CHRISTMAS FOR NEW SOUTH WALES EMERGENCY SERVICES
Emergency services throughout New South Wales are gearing up for a busy Christmas-New Year period.
While many of the state's workers are winding down for the summer break, emergency services are preparing for a rush of Christmas and New Year-related incidents.
All of the state's one-thousand Police Highway Patrol officers will be working during the period, blitzing motorists in Operation Safe Arrival.
All leave for Water Police has also been cancelled, with blanket supervision of the busy Sydney Harbour expected.
And, extra ambulance crews will be on hand to deal with New Years Eve incidents.
VICTORIAN BAT VIRUS WORRIES
Victoria's chief health officer says the discovery of the deadly Lyssavirus in a dead fruit bat in Melbourne's botanic gardens has prompted an alert on the state's bat colonies.
The Human Services Department is treating four people for possible exposure to the virus which claimed the life of a Rockhampton woman last month.
Dr Rouch says there is no indication the four have been infected with the Lyssavirus, but authorities have issued a general alert and extended research and testing.
He says the virus can only be transmitted through bites or scratches.
